industry.headline: UK's Under-16 Social Media Ban Still Has No Rulebook as Ofcom's October Deadline Looms
industry.summary: Nearly four months after the UK announced a bar on under-16 social media accounts, no implementing regulation exists yet, but Ofcom must report on 'highly effective' age-assurance methods by end of October. This is the exact regulatory track NOMO's CEO Leonardo has been engaging with in the UK, and the looming deadline is a near-term catalyst that could create an opening for NOMO to position its off-social rewards model as compliance-adjacent ahead of Spring 2027 rollout.

industry.headline: Long Island school districts continue to join lawsuits against social media companies
industry.summary: More Long Island districts (including Hicksville) voted to join mass-tort litigation against Meta, Snap, TikTok and YouTube over youth mental health harms, with school-district claims still unresolved even after Meta's proposed $17B AG settlement. School districts independently suing over screen-time-driven harms validates NOMO's core pitch and opens a window to position its incentive-based model as a constructive alternative to litigation in the US GTM push.

industry.headline: Philippine Senate passes bill banning under-18s from social media
industry.summary: The Senate passed a 16-1 vote restricting under-18 social media access, following a House bill setting the age floor at 13. A signal (exploratory region only for NOMO) that youth social-media restriction norms are spreading globally beyond NOMO's core UK/US/AU policy watch.

new_candidates.name: Dayo (Dayo Deals)
new_candidates.why_fits: Pays teens cash or brand gift cards (Starbucks, Adidas, Amazon) for staying under agreed screen-time limits since its Jan 2026 launch — a direct overlap with NOMO's reward-for-reduced-screen-time model and brand-partnership strategy.

new_candidates.name: Screen Free Time: Less is More
new_candidates.why_fits: Lets teens earn points for screen-free time and redeem them for a reward they personally chose — mirrors NOMO's Moments-to-real-reward loop almost point for point, and is actively being updated.

new_candidates.name: Fluid Focus
new_candidates.why_fits: Gamifies reduced screen time for rewards exactly like NOMO's core mechanic, and is expanding from the UK into the US — the same two markets NOMO is prioritizing, making it a competitor worth watching on both fronts.

new_candidates.name: ScrollStash
new_candidates.why_fits: Pays teens real cash for every hour spent off TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and 20+ other apps — a direct cash-reward rival in the same teen screen-time-reduction niche as NOMO, launched within the last month.

new_candidates.name: NuKase (NuGerm)
new_candidates.why_fits: Already embedded in 45+ school districts' phone-policy budgets with documented 96% compliance and a 61% drop in phone-related disciplinary referrals — competing for the same school-district device/behavior-management budget lines NOMO's Education vertical targets.

new_candidates.name: Togleam (Screen Time Chores)
new_candidates.why_fits: Uses a near-identical challenge-and-verification loop to NOMO's: kids complete real-world challenges with photo proof, parents approve, and screen time is granted — directly rivaling NOMO's challenge-based accountability mechanic.

new_candidates.name: Zenera
new_candidates.why_fits: A gamified focus app with streaks, a leaderboard, and real-world perks redeemable with focus points — a near-identical value proposition to NOMO's Moments/leaderboard/reward model, worth tracking even as an exploratory-region signal.

new_candidates.name: Forest
new_candidates.why_fits: Explicitly named in NOMO's own competitor-fit criteria but currently untracked — a mainstream gamified habit-builder (grow a tree by staying off your phone) competing for the same digital-wellbeing audience.

new_candidates.name: JOMO (Jomo - Screen Time Blocker)
new_candidates.why_fits: Also explicitly named in NOMO's competitor-fit criteria but untracked — an actively updated app-blocking tool competing for the same teen digital-wellbeing user base.

new_candidates.name: TDF (Theatre Development Fund) — Tickets for Teens
new_candidates.why_fits: A NYC municipal program giving high schoolers free/discounted Broadway and museum access via a digital membership card — the same 'ticket/museum access' reward category as Fever and Odeon, but through a city-government channel NOMO doesn't yet have.

new_candidates.name: Bank of America — Museums on Us
new_candidates.why_fits: A nationwide network offering free admission to 200+ museums on recurring weekends — scalable museum-ticket reward inventory that extends well beyond NOMO's current Fever and Odeon venue-based partners.

new_candidates.name: Planet Fitness (Teen Summer Pass program)
new_candidates.why_fits: Already runs a free-access pass for teens 14-19 across 2,400+ locations — realistic, scalable wellness-reward inventory alongside NOMO's Down Dog and Future partners, with a built-in teen audience.

new_candidates.name: MLB (via team Kids Club programs, e.g. Mariners/D-backs)
new_candidates.why_fits: Fills a clear sports-league gap in NOMO's roster (NFL, NBA, Premier League and Campeonato Brasileiro are covered, but not MLB) — clubs already run youth-club reward mechanics unlocking free tickets, a direct match to NOMO's ticket-reward model.

new_candidates.name: Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD)
new_candidates.why_fits: Unanimously approved a district-wide screen-time cap phasing in through 2026-27 — a concrete, time-sensitive procurement window for an off-screen rewards partner in the US's second-largest district, directly aligned with NOMO's US GTM push.

new_candidates.name: England state-funded schools phone-free mandate (UK Department for Education)
new_candidates.why_fits: Under the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026, England's state schools are now legally required to be phone-free, with an under-16 social media curfew moving toward 2027 — a government-mandated tailwind for a rewards-based off-screen program in NOMO's growing UK market, where its CEO is already engaged on policy.

new_candidates.name: Vitality (Discovery/Vitality Health)
new_candidates.why_fits: Just expanded its AI-driven health-incentive platform to the US via a Google partnership, rewarding behaviors including sleep and activity — a strong fit for the currently-empty insurance-vertical distribution lane and a timely, active US signal.

new_candidates.name: Active Minds
new_candidates.why_fits: Just received new Google.org funding to scale a national youth mental-health and digital-wellbeing program to 100,000 young people — a credible, large-scale community-trust partner for NOMO's Youth Orgs vertical, not currently represented in its GTM lineup.

new_candidates.name: Boys & Girls Clubs of America
new_candidates.why_fits: Just signed a two-year deal with Versant Media explicitly targeting 'digital and media literacy' and 'impactful real-world experiences' for teens — clear, demonstrated appetite for exactly the kind of GTM/rewards tie-in NOMO offers.

new_candidates.name: Pop Warner Little Scholars
new_candidates.why_fits: The largest youth football/cheer/dance organization (425,000+ kids) has no digital-wellness or screen-time partner, unlike its registration-tech partners (GameChanger, TeamSnap) — a genuine, unclaimed GTM gap in the youth-sports vertical.

new_candidates.name: SANDAG / County of San Diego (Youth Opportunity Pass)
new_candidates.why_fits: A municipal program already incentivizing youth engagement at scale — free transit for all riders 18 & under via a Youth PRONTO app account — a direct match for NOMO's Municipalities vertical and a live precedent for app-based youth incentive delivery.

new_candidates.name: Vitality Health (UK)
new_candidates.why_fits: The UK's leading insurer-run wellness rewards program, converting healthy activity into points redeemable with partner brands — a proven insurance-distribution model for digital-wellness incentives in the exact UK market where NOMO's CEO is already active on policy.

new_candidates.name: New York State Education Department (NYSED) / Distraction-Free Schools rollout
new_candidates.why_fits: New York's statewide law now requires bell-to-bell smartphone restrictions across all K-12 districts, with policies finalized by August 1 — a clear state-level implementation opportunity for NOMO's Municipalities & States vertical, not yet in its GTM pipeline.

rejected_today.name: Screen-Free Time: Less is More (Loyal Foundry, Inc.)
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the higher-confidence 'Screen Free Time: Less is More' entry; same app and mechanic already captured.
rejected_today.why_fits: An actively updated (last build ~44 days ago) teen-focused app where kids earn points for screen-free time and redeem them for parent-approved real rewards, structurally mirroring NOMO's Moments-for-offline-time and reward redemption mechanic.

rejected_today.category: Teen screen-time reward app with brand partnerships
rejected_today.name: Dayo Deals
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the 'Dayo (Dayo Deals)' entry; same company and mechanic already captured.
rejected_today.why_fits: Dayo is a parent-teen app that <cite index="10-2">enables parents to strike bargains with their teenage children—specifically to help them reduce their screen time and social media use</cite>, and <cite index="10-2">is working with Starbucks, Adidas, Amazon and other brands to help teens (and adults) manage their screen time</cite>, directly overlapping NOMO's reward-for-reduced-screen-time model and brand partnership strategy.

rejected_today.name: NuKase
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate entity captured more concretely as a Competitor (NuKase/NuGerm) with quantified results; redundant GTM framing of the same company.
rejected_today.why_fits: Helps K-12 districts navigate and apply for new state phone-free-schools grants before deadlines, positioning it inside the exact wave of state cellphone-ban funding and procurement cycles that NOMO's Education vertical (João, Direct) targets for district-level partnerships.

rejected_today.name: Screen-Free Time (Loyal Foundry)
rejected_today.reason: Third duplicate of the 'Screen Free Time: Less is More' app already captured at higher confidence.
rejected_today.why_fits: A recently published teen-focused app where teens earn points for screen-free time and redeem them toward a parent-approved real-world reward, using badges, streaks, and goal-paths — a near-direct feature match to NOMO's core loop.

rejected_today.name: Goode Foundation Digital Detox Challenge
rejected_today.reason: A cash-incentive nonprofit program rather than a scalable tech product; weak match to NOMO's app-based competitor fit bar.
rejected_today.why_fits: A foundation-run program that pays students (7th–9th graders) cash for giving up smartphones/social media through a school year — a direct, if lower-tech, rival model to NOMO's reward-for-screen-time-reduction value proposition targeting the same teen demographic.

rejected_today.name: NYC Culture Pass / IDNYC
rejected_today.reason: Redundant with TDF Tickets for Teens — another NYC-specific museum/culture pass covering the same reward category and city.
rejected_today.why_fits: A municipally-backed teen-eligible (13+) free pass program unlocking 100+ museums, gardens and cultural venues — matches the 'museum tickets / city green pass' reward archetype NOMO already runs with Fever, but via a civic/municipal channel not yet represented in the lineup.

rejected_today.name: Schools Beyond Screens
rejected_today.reason: Its own why_fits flags an anti-corporate-sponsorship stance as a real partnership risk, undermining fit as a brand/rewards GTM partner.
rejected_today.why_fits: A fast-growing grassroots coalition now advocating inside 217 school districts across 40 states for intentional, evidence-based classroom tech policy — a potential high-leverage channel into João's 6-12 Education vertical beyond named districts like LAUSD/NYC DOE, though its explicitly anti-corporate-sponsorship stance is a real partnership risk to vet.

rejected_today.name: Missouri Department of Mental Health (Digital Detox Challenge)
rejected_today.reason: Single-state program is marginal next to stronger, higher-confidence state/municipal candidates (LAUSD, NYSED, SANDAG) already covering this vertical.
rejected_today.why_fits: A state Department of Mental Health runs its own multi-week 'Digital Detox Challenge' promoting screen-time reduction statewide — exactly the kind of state-level decision-maker Leo's Municipalities/States vertical targets, and a live example of a public body already running screen-time programming that NOMO could power or co-brand.

rejected_today.name: YMCA (Y.O.U. / Cleveland YMCA teen partnership model)
rejected_today.reason: Redundant with the higher-confidence Boys & Girls Clubs of America entry in the same Youth Orgs vertical; weaker single-chapter evidence.
rejected_today.why_fits: YMCA locations are actively building paid, structured teen engagement programs (ages 14-18) focused on well-being and real-world experiences, and YMCA's national app already runs an 'earn points / redeem rewards / join challenges' structure — signaling organizational readiness for a NOMO-style gamified off-screen rewards integration at the community level.

rejected_today.name: Urban Air Adventure Park / Unleashed Brands (KidHub)
rejected_today.reason: Audience skews younger/family rather than NOMO's core teen/Gen Z demographic; weaker reward-fit match.
rejected_today.why_fits: Urban Air is actively distributing app-exclusive free unlimited play passes through a youth-focused app (KidHub) as an acquisition tool, proving the exact 'tradeable reward inventory delivered through a youth app' mechanic NOMO uses, with passes valid for 45 days and aimed at family/teen audiences.

rejected_today.name: TRUCE Family
rejected_today.reason: Overlaps with other school device-management/compliance tools; redundant with NuKase's stronger, quantified evidence.
rejected_today.why_fits: District-partnered app for managing device use, directly competing for school EdTech partnerships in NOMO's core vertical, as seen with Lancaster School District: "we are introducing a new partnership with TRUCE FAMILY, a mobile app that will create and maintain distraction-free classrooms."

rejected_today.name: LockedIn
rejected_today.reason: Overlaps with other school device-management/compliance tools already represented by NuKase; redundant to avoid duplicating the same competitive theme.
rejected_today.why_fits: Directly competes for school district contracts by offering compliance enforcement for phone-free laws: "LockedIn provides automated, OS-level enforcement on every student's existing phone with no hardware required," overlapping with NOMO's Education vertical and app-block competitor criteria.

rejected_today.name: Culture Pass (NYC Public Libraries)
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the NYC Culture Pass/IDNYC concept and overlapping with TDF Tickets for Teens; same city, same reward category.
rejected_today.why_fits: Offers exactly the kind of tradeable museum-ticket inventory NOMO already uses (cf. Fever), bundled across 100+ institutions for a teen-eligible (13+) audience: "Culture Pass is a program for cardholding patrons 13 and older... get free admission to dozens of NYC cultural institutions."

rejected_today.name: Go City (attraction passes)
rejected_today.reason: Its own why_fits notes it is similar in spirit to existing partner GetYourGuide — too similar to an existing partner to add distinct value.
rejected_today.why_fits: Sells bundled access to dozens of city attractions (museums, tours, sights) across major markets, similar in spirit to GetYourGuide and Fever already in NOMO's lineup, and offers a scalable, tradeable ticket inventory well suited to teen/Gen Z redemption rewards.

rejected_today.name: Oscar Health (Oscar Unlocks)
rejected_today.reason: Redundant with the higher-confidence Vitality (US) entry in the same insurance wellness-rewards vertical.
rejected_today.why_fits: Oscar unveiled 'Oscar Unlocks' for 2026, a rewards program letting ACA plan members earn badges, perks, and rewards for healthy behaviors — a live example of an insurer building exactly the kind of digital-wellness incentive infrastructure NOMO could plug into, filling the currently-empty insurance GTM lane.

rejected_today.name: UK Department for Science, Innovation & Technology (under-16 social media ban rollout)
rejected_today.reason: Overlaps with the England phone-free schools mandate candidate and the industry item on the UK under-16 ban; redundant regulatory story.
rejected_today.why_fits: Aligns with NOMO's flagged UK region weighting (CEO impacting UK/US/AU policy): the UK government announced a ban on social media for under-16s modeled on Australia's, with regulations expected before Parliament and the ban "coming into effect from spring 2027" — a national policy implementation partner opportunity ahead of enforcement, distinct from any current GTM partner.

rejected_today.name: Busch Gardens / United Parks & Resorts (Annual Pass program)
rejected_today.reason: Generic theme-park ticket offer overlapping with existing experience-reward partners (GetYourGuide, Fever); not differentiated enough to add.
rejected_today.why_fits: Fits the tradeable-ticket-inventory, teen/Gen Z-friendly criteria used for existing partners like GetYourGuide and Odeon; the newly launched 2026 Annual Pass program offers "unlimited admission, exclusive perks, and first access to new rides" plus free guest tickets — realistic, scalable reward inventory not yet represented in NOMO's current lineup.

rejected_today.category: Teen multi-venue culture/experience pass (movies, music, theatre, dance, visual art)
rejected_today.name: TeenTix
rejected_today.reason: Overlaps with TDF Tickets for Teens and Bank of America Museums on Us; another generic teen culture-access pass with lower differentiation.
rejected_today.why_fits: TeenTix offers <cite index="35-4">a FREE TeenTix Pass to get into movies, music, theatre, dance, visual art, and more for just $5</cite>, with <cite index="35-9,35-10">thousands of teenagers who use TeenTix every month... good until your 20th birthday</cite> — a teen-dedicated, multi-category cultural access pass that fills a gap versus NOMO's single-venue partners (Odeon, Ingresso, Fever) by bundling several experience categories a teen audience already trusts.
